blocks.content: Find the **Support calls** panel. It shows one large number, a stat. This panel answers the question: What is the value over this time range? Here, the value is the average number of support calls. The stat uses the **Mean** calculation, so the big number is an average, not the current value. A stat set to **Last** would show the current value. The faint line beneath the number sketches how the value moved, but the number is what you take in at a glance.
Focus on **Sign ups**, another stat panel. This panel answers the same question for sign ups. The value is the average number of sign ups over the time range, also calculated with **Mean**.

Next, focus on **server requests**, a time series panel.

This panel answers the question: How has this value gone up and down over time? Here, the value is the number of requests the server handles.

A stat would reduce those values to one number and hide the pattern. A stat suits a key metric to check at a glance. But when you need the trend, a time series says more.
